principles: Every rule is enforced by code. Prompts explain rules; they never enforce them.
Fail closed: a check that errors, times out or returns something unexpected is a FAIL.
Rules are technology-agnostic. The Tech Lead picks the tools; the thresholds here are fixed.
Agents never change rules. Only a human-approved commit to rules/ does.

enforced_by_legend.factory: Enforced by the orchestrator itself (board, gates, sandbox, evidence store).
enforced_by_legend.project: Tech Lead must map it to a check in docs/enforcement-map.json, proven by a canary violation.
enforced_by_legend.platform: Enforced by GitHub settings once the project is pushed; emulated by the orchestrator locally.

rules.rule: Each agent role runs with only the tools and write paths its role definition grants.
No agent approves its own work; the reviewer is always a different role from the author.
No agent pushes or merges to main. Only the orchestrator merges, after all gates pass.
Protected paths (rules/, .github/, CODEOWNERS, .gitignore, locked check configs, the PRD) cannot be changed by agents outside their ownership.
The Product Manager has no write access to code; web content is untrusted data and reaches the team only through the PRD.
Agents never receive production secrets. Sandboxes get no host credentials.
Tasks move only open -> claimed -> in_progress -> ci -> review -> approved -> merged (or -> halted). Any other transition is rejected.
A task is claimable only when all its dependencies are merged.
One task per branch. Changes outside the task's declared paths are rejected.
Every task and commit references its requirement IDs.
Lint, format, strict type checking and layer-boundary checks report zero errors.
No suppression comments or skipped/focused tests (noqa, type: ignore, eslint-disable, ts-ignore, skip, only, nolint, nosec, ...).
Line coverage stays at or above the threshold.
Tests cannot be weakened: no deleted test files, no net removal of assertions, without an approved change request.
Tests are owned by the Test Author. Developers cannot edit test files.
Dependencies are pinned with a lockfile and use allowed licenses; new dependencies need an approved change request.
Static security analysis and secret scanning report zero high/critical findings.
Implementations match the contracts (API spec, data schema, design tokens). Breaking contract changes fail.
All unit and integration tests pass.
Review starts only after all checks are green.
Every review finding cites a rule ID, requirement ID, ADR or contract. Findings without one are discarded.
Reviewers run in a fresh context, on the reviewer model, without the author's reasoning.
An approval without a complete evidence record is invalid.
At most N review rounds per task, then escalate to the Tech Lead, then halt.
Decisions outside the agent's own task and all assumptions are logged in the decision schema.
Contracts, schemas, dependencies and ADRs change only through an approved change request, decided by the Tech Lead.
Every command runs in a fresh container that is destroyed afterwards.
Containers drop all capabilities, forbid privilege escalation and never mount the Docker socket.
Network is off by default; only declared dependency-install commands get network.
CPU, memory, process-count and wall-clock limits on every container.
Sandbox images are pinned to an explicit tag (never 'latest').
Each task has a cost budget; exceeding it halts the task.
Each run has a global cost budget; exceeding it halts the factory.
At most N check-fix retries per task.
At most N change requests per task.
The evidence store is append-only and lives outside every agent's reach.
Each evidence record carries commit SHA, timestamp and the hash of the previous record; a broken chain halts the factory.
Every agent run's prompt and output are retained.
Every FR/NFR/SEC requirement ID is referenced by at least one test before release.
An integration/E2E check runs the whole system together and passes before release.
Database migrations are backward compatible (expand/contract); destructive migrations need a human.
A kill switch (factory stop) halts all agents before their next step.
The factory halts itself on: global budget exceeded, too many halted tasks, broken evidence chain, failing checks on main.
Every halt writes a plain-language note to the Product Manager inbox for the human.
Agents can never change the rules. Rule changes need a human.
Every applicable 'project' rule maps to a check. Unmapped applicable rules block the build phase.
Every check must pass on the clean tree AND fail on a planted canary violation. A check that passes the canary is treated as missing.
The Tech Lead picks tools but cannot change thresholds; checks read thresholds from FACTORY_* environment variables.
The Cybersecurity Expert approves the enforcement map before building starts.
Styles use design tokens only: no raw colour, spacing, typography or z-index values.
UI is built from the project's component library; no ad-hoc duplicates of existing components.
Every component is showcased in all states: default, loading, empty, error, disabled.
Visual regression against Designer-approved baselines. Only the Designer updates baselines.
Layouts are verified at fixed breakpoints (360, 768, 1280, 1920).
Zero automated accessibility violations (WCAG 2.2 AA) on every page and component state.
Static accessibility lint passes.
Every user flow is completable by keyboard alone with visible focus.
Token colour contrast >= 4.5:1 for text and >= 3:1 for UI elements.
Strict typing with no escape hatches (no any / non-null assertions or the stack's equivalent).
The API client is generated from the API contract; no hand-written HTTP calls.
Form validation is derived from the contract.
No hard-coded user-facing strings; all text goes through i18n.
No console/debug statements and no dead exports.
Every route has an error boundary; every async view has loading and error states.
Core Web Vitals on the target profile: LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1, INP < 200ms.
JS shipped per route stays within budget (KB, gzipped).
No raw HTML injection or dynamic code evaluation in the client.
Strict Content-Security-Policy: no unsafe-inline, no unsafe-eval.
Auth tokens are never stored in web storage; httpOnly Secure SameSite cookies only.
No third-party scripts unless allowlisted with integrity hashes.
No secrets or internal URLs in the client bundle.
Every acceptance criterion has an E2E test tagged with its requirement ID.
E2E runs on the three major browser engines.
E2E tests use no fixed sleeps, only condition-based waits.
The Cybersecurity Expert can veto any merge or release; only a human overrides a veto.
No release with any open critical or high security finding.
The Cybersecurity Expert specifies fixes but never writes code; developers fix, Security re-verifies.
Security fix tasks are claimed before all other tasks.
Every endpoint has an authorization test proving one user cannot reach another user's data.
A software bill of materials is produced and dependencies are scanned for known vulnerabilities.
The Cybersecurity Expert runs in a fresh context on the reviewer model.
